html:
The Kasubi Tombs on a hill in Kampala are the burial place of four kings of Buganda, built in 1882 as the palace of Kabaka Muteesa I and turned into his tomb when he died in 1884.

The main building, Muzibu Azaala Mpanga, was a huge round house of wooden poles, reeds and thatch, one of the finest buildings in this tradition. Later kings, among them Mutesa II, the first president of Uganda, were buried beside Muteesa I.

UNESCO listed the tombs in 2001. In March 2010 the main building burned down, causing grief and protest across Buganda, and it was rebuilt with traditional methods. The tombs are a centre of the kingdom's religion and identity in Kampala.
sum: The Kasubi Tombs on a hill in Kampala are the burial place of four kings of Buganda, built in 1882 as the palace of Kabaka Muteesa I and turned into his tomb when he died in 1884.
